entries.source_title: Il/elle/ils/elles = it/he/she/they (French Subject Pronouns)
entries.note: Grammatical reference for things and people is already explicit, including female-only and mixed groups; the mapped substitution tasks require those decisions rather than just recalling a pronoun list.

entries.source_title: On can mean either we/one/people (French Subject Pronouns)
entries.note: The existing meanings of on were adequate. Added the missing distinction between its singular verb and an adjective agreeing with a known group.

entries.source_title: Using nous/vous/ils/elles to replace compound subjects (French Subject Pronouns)
entries.note: The speaker-first, listener-next decision for a compound subject is already worked through and tested for nous, vous and mixed third-person reference.

entries.source_title: Nous vs on to say "we" in French (French Subject Pronouns)
entries.note: Conversational on versus nous was already practised. Added bidirectional rewrites showing that the verb changes while a known group's adjective agreement can remain.

entries.source_title: "C'est" vs "Il/Elle est" to say it is/she is/he is in French
entries.note: Identification with a noun phrase, bare-profession description and overall evaluation are already distinguished with bilingual examples and constrained production. No wholesale rewrite was needed.

entries.source_title: C'est, ce sont = this is, these are (French Demonstrative Pronouns)
entries.note: Added a worked distinction between plural noun identification and evaluating a plural-named topic as a whole; an intervening adverb does not erase the noun phrase.

entries.source_title: Ça = that/this/it (French Demonstrative Pronouns)
entries.note: The existing demonstrative meaning was sufficient. Added singular verb agreement after ça even when the detached topic is plural, contrasted with tracking those things using elles.

entries.source_title: Moi/toi/lui/elle = Me/you/him/her - simple cases (French Stress Pronouns)
entries.note: The full stressed-pronoun set, isolated answers, emphasis and prepositional use already have examples and constructed responses; these meet the public body's instructional need.

entries.source_title: Nous/vous/eux/elles = Us/you/them - simple cases (French Stress Pronouns)
entries.note: Plural stressed forms were already taught. Added the fixed identification c'est nous/vous in the reference lesson so learners do not manufacture ce sommes or ce êtes.

entries.source_title: Penser que/Croire que = To think that/To believe that in French
entries.note: The affirmative thought-clause construction already keeps que/qu', supplies a full clause and contrasts penser à. The exercises assess the link, not an English word-for-word omission.

entries.source_title: Me/te/nous/vous = Me/you/us/you (French Direct and Indirect Object Pronouns)
entries.note: The existing direct/indirect explanation, elision, placement before the relevant verb and unchanged subject agreement cover the public scope with independent pronoun-placement work.

entries.source_title: Tout le monde = Everybody/Everyone (French Indefinite Pronouns)
entries.note: Singular agreement was already secure. Added everyone in the relevant situation versus the geographical whole world, with both reference choice and sentence transformation.

entries.source_title: Conjugate avoir in the present tense in French (Le Présent)
entries.note: Avoir already has its complete present paradigm, elision, possession and age uses, plus multiple-person production and correction. No useful teaching gap remained.

entries.source_title: Conjugate être in the present tense in French (Le Présent)
entries.note: Être already has a complete accented paradigm and examples linking subjects to identity or description. Mapped production checks include forms that cannot be guessed from a regular ending.

entries.source_title: Conjugate aller in the present tense in French (Le Présent)
entries.note: Aller already has all six persons, its irregular stems and location use; several independent items prevent treating its -er infinitive as a regular conjugation.

entries.source_title: Conjugate venir/tenir and derivatives in the present tense in French (Le Présent)
entries.note: Both complete base paradigms and meaningful prefix transfer are already taught. Extending the lexical catalogue would add length rather than a missing conjugation decision.

entries.source_title: Conjugate regular -er verbs in the present tense in French (Le Présent)
entries.note: The complete regular -er model, stem-plus-ending method and subject-specific writing checks already support transfer beyond the model verb.

entries.source_title: Expressing current actions, habits and situations (English Present Tense) with the present tense (Le Présent) in French
entries.note: Present habits, states and current events are already separated from English auxiliary habits; the mapped tasks require interpreting and forming the appropriate present.

entries.source_title: Conjugate faire in the present tense in French (Le Présent)
entries.note: Faire already has a full paradigm, doing/making contexts and explicit attention to vous faites and ils font, with independent production across persons.

entries.source_title: Conjugate vouloir in the present tense in French (Le Présent)
entries.note: Vouloir's full paradigm and infinitive complement are already explained and practised without inserting a preposition or conjugating the second verb.

entries.source_title: Conjugate pouvoir in the present tense in French (Le Présent)
entries.note: The complete pouvoir paradigm, ability/permission meanings and constrained infinitive pattern are already present, with the formal puis variant explicitly distinguished from ordinary peux.

entries.source_title: Conjugate devoir in the present tense in French (Le Présent)
entries.note: Devoir's full paradigm and requirement-plus-infinitive pattern already meet this conjugation body's scope. The separate need/owe comparison receives its own depth record.

entries.source_title: Conjugate regular -ir verbs in the present tense in French (Le Présent)
entries.note: Added a dictionary-word check using répartir versus repartir and a sound-versus-spelling explanation, building on the existing full -ir paradigm rather than implying that all -ir verbs behave alike.

entries.source_title: Conjugate regular -dre verbs in the present tense in French (Le Présent)
entries.note: The existing regular -dre model and exclusion of other families were sufficient. Added the audible-d contrast and a written singular-form decision so silent endings are not guessed from sound alone.

entries.source_title: Conjugate croire in the present tense in French (Le Présent)
entries.note: The actual public article is example-led; our lesson already supplies the complete croire paradigm, plural-stem explanation and meaningful complement contrast with production evidence.

entries.source_title: Conjugate semi-regular -cer verbs in the present tense in French (Le Présent)
entries.note: The reason for ç before -ons, the complete commencer paradigm and transfer to another -cer verb are already visible and assessed.

entries.source_title: Conjugate semi-regular -ger verbs in the present tense in French (Le Présent)
entries.note: The preserved soft-g explanation, complete manger paradigm and plural-context construction already explain why only nous needs the extra e in these present forms.

entries.source_title: Conjugate reflexive verbs in the present tense in French (Le Présent)
entries.note: Subject-matched reflexive pronouns, elision and ordinary conjugation are already integrated in full paradigms, examples and pronoun-production tasks.

entries.source_title: Conjugate reflexive verb se réveiller in the present tense in French (Le Présent)
entries.note: Se réveiller already has complete forms and is meaningfully distinguished from getting up; mapped items test its reflexive spelling and subject matching.

entries.source_title: Conjugate reflexive verb se lever in the present tense in French (Le Présent)
entries.note: Se lever already combines the full reflexive paradigm with the e/è alternation and the distinction from merely waking. Independent items assess the relevant changes.

entries.source_title: Conjugate reflexive verb se coucher in the present tense in French (Le Présent)
entries.note: Se coucher already has full forms and the useful limit that going to bed is not necessarily falling asleep. Existing production covers the reflexive and plural forms.

entries.source_title: Conjugate reflexive verb s'habiller in the present tense in French (Le Présent)
entries.note: S'habiller already explains silent-h elision and supplies every person, including the non-elided plural reflexive pronouns, with independent construction checks.

entries.source_title: Conjugate reflexive verb se laver in the present tense in French (Le Présent)
entries.note: Se laver is already the full system model and is connected to obvious-body-part articles. The mapped tasks exercise the actual pronoun/verb combination.

entries.source_title: Conjugate reflexive verb s'amuser in the present tense in French (Le Présent)
entries.note: S'amuser already has its own meaning, complete forms and elision, rather than being only a named example of reflexive verbs.

entries.source_title: Conjugate -é(-)er, -e(-)er verbs - except -eter and -eler - in the present tense in French (Le Présent)
entries.note: Existing e/é-to-è paradigms were good. Added the boundary that a circumflex is not that alternation, with a full rêver paradigm and contrastive written decisions.

entries.source_title: Conjugate partir/sortir and other irregular -TIR verbs in the present tense in French (Le Présent)
entries.note: The full short-stem paradigms and prefix strategy were already present. Cross-linked evidence now tests the meaningful répartir/repartir boundary instead of transferring a family merely by resemblance.

entries.source_title: Conjugate -eter and -eler verbs in the present tense in French (Le Présent) - main rule (ll / tt)
entries.note: The existing lesson already distinguishes appeler/jeter from acheter/geler and explicitly preserves both traditional and rectified alternatives for other applicable verbs. No variant was removed.

entries.source_title: Conjugate prendre and derivatives in the present tense in French (Le Présent)
entries.note: Prendre and its derivatives already have the full stem changes, including plural d loss and nn, with several independent family-transfer items.

entries.source_title: Expressing ongoing actions (English Present Continuous) with the present tense (Le Présent) in French
entries.note: The ordinary French present already covers current action without adding être, and the lesson directly corrects the English auxiliary calque with independent production.

entries.source_title: Conjugate dire and derivatives in the present tense in French (Le Présent)
entries.note: The full dire model already distinguishes redire, other -disez derivatives and the separate maudire plural. Existing exercises genuinely test those boundaries.

entries.source_title: Conjugate dormir and other -MIR verbs in the present tense in French (Le Présent)
entries.note: Added the missing semantic decision between sleeping, falling asleep and putting someone to sleep, retaining the familiar conjugation and supplying the complete s'endormir paradigm.

entries.source_title: Conjugate écrire/inscrire in the present tense in French (Le Présent)
entries.note: Écrire and inscrire already have complete paradigms, plural v and accented spellings, plus meaningful message/address contexts and independent derivative production.

entries.source_title: Expressing immediate and near-future actions with the present tense (Le Présent) in French
entries.note: The present's future reading is already tied to scheduling and time context, not treated as an automatic future meaning. Existing items distinguish that use from a near-future construction.

entries.source_title: Conjugate verbs in the near future in French using aller + infinitive (Le Futur Proche)
entries.note: The full aller-plus-infinitive formation, negation, motion contrast and absence of a fixed elapsed-time cutoff already supply useful depth and application.

entries.source_title: Conjugate lire in the present tense in French (Le Présent)
entries.note: Added relire and élire as meaningful transfer cases, with complete paradigms and independent rereading/election contexts; the prefix changes meaning, not the lire endings.

entries.source_title: Conjugate reflexive verbs in the near future in French using aller + infinitive (Le Futur Proche)
entries.note: The existing lesson already keeps the reflexive pronoun with the infinitive, selects it for the subject, handles elision and explains negative order with real production.

entries.source_title: Expressing the close past in French using "venir de" + [infinitive] (Le Passé Proche)
entries.note: Recent completion, full venir forms, de/d', reflexive placement and the origin-versus-completed-action contrast are already taught and tested. The optional emphatic adverb does not require another formation model.

entries.source_title: Conjugate mettre and derivatives in the present tense in French (Le Présent)
entries.note: Mettre already has its complete paradigm, singular/plural stems, prefix transfer and the practical putting-on versus wearing contrast with independent application.

entries.source_title: Conjugate -eter and -eler verbs in the present tense in French (Le Présent) - with "è"
entries.note: Complete acheter/geler models and contrasts with doubling verbs are already explicit. The existing treatment preserves the published spelling variants without cloning a rare-verb catalogue.

entries.source_title: Conjugate reflexive verb s'asseoir in the present tense in French (Le Présent)
entries.note: Both standard s'asseoir series and both accepted infinitive spellings are already visible and accepted where relevant. No published variant was narrowed.

entries.source_title: Conjugate boire in the present tense in French (Le Présent)
entries.note: Boire's three present stems, complete paradigm and independent singular/plural production already address the public body's conjugation need.

entries.source_title: Du/de la/de l'/des = Some/any (French Partitive Articles)
entries.note: Existing portion/category teaching was strong. Added an explicit same-noun count-versus-material decision and practice that cannot be solved merely by memorising a food noun's gender.

entries.source_title: Definite articles contract with à and de in French (French Contracted Articles)
entries.note: All four contractions and the noncontracting la/l' cases are already contrasted; the lesson also distinguishes contracted du from a partitive reading.

entries.source_title: Continents/countries/counties/regions/states are masculine, feminine or plural in French (Gender)
entries.note: Gender clues and named exceptions were already supplied. Added a whole-name decision using singular pays de Galles so visible final s is not mistaken for grammatical plurality.

entries.source_title: Using le, la, l', les with continents, countries & regions names (definite articles)
entries.note: The article inventory already includes country/region gender, articleless names and city-name exceptions. The existing examples avoid treating every city or country alike.

entries.source_title: En/l'/au with seasons (French Articles and Prepositions)
entries.note: Seasonal genders, au printemps versus en with the other seasons, and general/recurring definite-article use are already explained and exercised.

entries.source_title: Using le, la, l', les before nouns when generalising (definite articles)
entries.note: Added category versus particular liked referent and English zero-article contrasts, plus general negative retention versus zero quantity. No blanket claim that preference verbs force definite articles was introduced.

entries.source_title: Identifying the gender of nouns by some specific word endings in French
entries.note: Added useful -isme, -té/-tié and quality-noun -eur clues with explicit exceptions and a noun-plus-gender verification method. No unsupported success percentage or universal suffix rule was imported.

entries.source_title: Using "le" with days of the week + the weekend (French Definite Articles)
entries.note: The recurring/bare weekday contrast was already good. Added a full dated weekday and a subject use to show why le does not always mean every.

entries.source_title: Using le, la, les with weights and measures (definite articles)
entries.note: Per-unit prices already use the definite article with single items, kilos and a multi-gram quantity. Existing items test the rate relation rather than possession.

entries.source_title: Forming the plural of French nouns ending in -au or -eau
entries.note: Retained the existing -x pattern with landaus and validated sarraus exceptions. The public body's unconditional -au pattern does not justify deleting the published exception.

references.purpose: The dictionary explicitly gives sarraus; preserve that published exception rather than adopting an unconditional -au to -aux rule.

entries.source_title: Using le, la, les with body parts and clothing (definite articles)
entries.note: The obvious-owner article rule was already taught with clothing limits. Added lever la main versus se lever so learners do not create a reflexive verb merely to translate your.

entries.source_title: Using le, la, les with titles, languages and academic subjects (definite articles)
entries.note: Added explicit acceptance of parler le français alongside common parler français; kept the existing subject-language article and direct-address contrast rather than rewriting them as absolute bans.

entries.source_title: Forming the plural of French nouns ending in -al
entries.note: The usual -al to -aux change and common -s exceptions already have noun headwords, examples and independent spelling checks; related -ail is not conflated.

entries.source_title: Forming the plural of French nouns ending in -eu
entries.note: The existing -eu model and pneus/bleus exceptions are already practised with written plural production, so the public body revealed no useful gap.

entries.source_title: Surnames don't pluralise in French
entries.note: Ordinary family surnames already remain unchanged, with the historical-family qualification retained. Mapped questions assess the intended ordinary use rather than inventing a universal rule.

entries.source_title: Adjectives ending with mute -e don't change in the feminine in French
entries.note: The basic agreement section already explains that silent final e needs no second e, while plural agreement remains available, with independent adjective production.

entries.source_title: Colour descriptions change according to gender and number (French Colour Adjectives)
entries.note: Existing simple, compound and noun-colour rules were sound. Added full brun agreement versus invariable colour marron, including agreement after être.

entries.source_title: Standalone adjectives after c'est are always masculine
entries.note: The standalone masculine-singular evaluation was already explained. Added a plural-topic contrast to prevent changing c'est merely because several things are under discussion.

entries.source_title: Expressing possession in French with "de"
entries.note: The thing-first, owner-second construction, contractions and elision already have contextual examples and production. No English possessive apostrophe calque is encouraged.

entries.source_title: Mon, ma, mes; ton, ta, tes; son, sa, ses = my; your; his / her in French (French possessive adjectives)
entries.note: All singular-owner possessive forms are already taught by the possessed noun's gender/number, including feminine vowel-initial nouns and owner-versus-object contrasts.

entries.source_title: Notre / nos / votre / vos / leur / leurs = our / your / their (French Possessive Adjectives)
entries.note: Notre/votre/leur and plural forms already distinguish possessor from possession, polite vous and shared/distributive contexts with constructed responses.

entries.source_title: Forming the feminine of nouns and adjectives ending in "-ien/-ion/-on" in French
entries.note: Existing feminine families include adjective and person/animal noun limits. Added nationality person-noun capitals versus descriptive adjectives and language names, with explicitly case-sensitive checks.

entries.source_title: Adjectives ending in -eux become -euse in the feminine in French
entries.note: The -eux/-euse family and separate -x pairs are already distinguished, with gender/number production rather than a misleading all-x replacement rule.

entries.source_title: Adjectives ending in -s or -x change in the plural forms only when feminine in French
entries.note: The unchanged masculine plural of -s/-x and the separately inflected feminine plural are already explicit and assessed.

entries.source_title: Beau, nouveau, vieux, fou, mou have two masculine forms and one feminine form (French Adjectives)
entries.note: The complete special adjective forms already specify immediate pre-noun vowel context, ordinary post-noun forms and the literary limits of fol/mol. Published nuance remains intact.

entries.source_title: Neuf vs nouveau to say new in French
entries.note: The second-hand/new-to-me distinction was already good. Added people and adopted animals to show why new in a situation does not mean unused or newly born.

entries.source_title: Forming regular adverbs with "-ment" in French (French Adverbs)
entries.note: Adverb formation already includes feminine-base and vowel cases, exceptions, invariant use and placement; the mapped tasks require independently constructing forms.

entries.source_title: Forming the feminine of adjectives ending in "-el/-eil/-il/-ul/-et/some in -s" in French
entries.note: The existing families retain explicit -il/-ul/-et/-s exceptions and their production checks. The public comparison did not warrant replacing these safeguards with a single doubling recipe.

entries.source_title: Beau, nouveau, vieux have different plural forms for masculine and feminine (French Adjectives)
entries.note: Masculine/feminine plurals of beau, nouveau and vieux are already fully listed, contrasted with special singular forms and tested in noun phrases.

entries.source_title: Adjectives ending in -er become -ère in the feminine in French
entries.note: The -er/-ère family and plural agreement already have visible examples and independent written production, including the accent.

entries.source_title: Position of French Adjectives - More adjectives that go BEFORE nouns
entries.note: Added count-before-rank grouping and descriptive adjective placement before a personal name; existing ordinary noun placement and plural de guidance remain intact.

entries.source_title: Ne ... pas = Not - with simple tenses (French Negations)
entries.note: Conjugated-verb bracketing, n' elision and informal ne omission versus standard written production are already clearly separated.

entries.source_title: Un/une become de/d' in negative sentences in French (French Indefinite Articles)
entries.note: Zero-quantity versus identification was already taught. Added what a subject does not become/remain so article retention is understood by meaning beyond a memorised être exception.

entries.source_title: Du/de la/de l'/des all become de/d' in negative sentences (French Partitive Articles)
entries.note: Added a denied-substance-transformation contrast to the existing absent-quantity rule, keeping the partitive when it describes the subject's resulting identity.

entries.source_title: Using "si" instead of "oui" to disagree with a negative question or statement in French
entries.note: The existing response section distinguishes contradicting a negative with si from confirming it with non, with both meaningful examples and constrained responses.

entries.source_title: Ne ... jamais = Never (French Negations)
entries.note: Jamais replacing pas in a negative habit is already explained, including reflexive placement and the limit that other uses belong to later study.

entries.source_title: Non plus = Neither/nor (French Negations)
entries.note: Sharing a negative fact with non plus is already contrasted with positive aussi, including standalone stressed-pronoun response and sentence placement.

entries.source_title: Ne ... pas = Not - with reflexive verbs in simple tenses (French Negations)
entries.note: Reflexive pronouns already remain between ne and the finite verb, with both pas and jamais examples and independently assessed word order.

entries.source_title: Position of French Negations - with conjugated verb + infinitive
entries.note: Added a same-action permission contrast between ne pouvez pas and pouvez ne pas, plus reflexive infinitive placement, so moving the negative changes a worked meaning rather than only word order.

entries.source_title: C'est quoi, Qu'est-ce que c'est ? = What's that? (French Questions)
entries.note: Object identity questions were already taught. Added polite repetition repair and the contextual Comment ? meaning, distinguished from identifying an object and from potentially abrupt Quoi ?.

entries.source_title: Asking yes/no questions in French with intonation, est-ce que, n'est-ce pas (French Questions)
entries.note: Statement order, est-ce que, conventional inversion, register and question punctuation already have visible models and independently constrained questions. Published sensitivity flags remain untouched.

entries.source_title: Asking questions in French with "qui/que/quoi/quand/où/comment/pourquoi/combien" (French Question Words)
entries.note: The information-word inventory already follows the missing-information decision, including subject qui, quoi after a preposition and combien de; questions constrain the expected construction fairly.

entries.source_title: Dans/sur/sous/devant/derrière/entre = in/on top of/under/in front of/behind/between (French Prepositions of Location)
entries.note: The spatial relations already have actual layouts, direct versus de-bearing prepositions and movement/location examples with independent selection and production.

entries.source_title: En vs Dans with locations (French Prepositions of Location)
entries.note: The existing activity/setting versus physical-interior contrast explains en classe versus dans la classe and explicitly rejects a gender-only shortcut.

entries.source_title: À côté de, en face de, à l'extérieur de, à l'intérieur de, près de, loin de, au coin de (French Prepositions)
entries.note: Added physical outside versus exception readings of en dehors de. Also narrowly corrected the mixed-language phrase en face du shop to en face du magasin; existing section identity and examples were preserved.

entries.source_title: Pour + [infinitive] = In order to + [do] in French
entries.note: Added subject-matched reflexive purpose and more formal afin de/d' while preserving the same-understood-doer boundary of the existing pour construction.

entries.source_title: En/au/aux = In/to with countries and continents (French Prepositions)
entries.note: Country location/destination and origin are already explained through gender, initial sound and number, with articleless exceptions; a short decision method is already practised.

entries.source_title: En/Dans = in/to + regions/states/counties (French Prepositions)
entries.note: Added an explicit canton-versus-city identity method rather than guessing a regional construction from a city name. Existing en/dans and au/dans regional variants remain accepted.

entries.source_title: À = To/in and De = From/of with cities in French (French Prepositions of Location)
entries.note: Ordinary à/de city constructions already include proper-name article contractions and the Quebec City/province distinction, avoiding an all-cities-have-no-article rule.

entries.source_title: Venir de/d'/du/des = To come/be from with countries/states/regions and continents (French Prepositions)
entries.note: The existing origin constructions distinguish country and regional article behaviour, include vowel cases and keep the city/province distinction visible in practice.

entries.source_title: À/en + [means of transportation] (French Prepositions)
entries.note: Existing mode-versus-position and cycling variants were strong. Added established par le train/par avion alternatives with their different article patterns, not a universal substitution rule.

entries.source_title: Differences between French and English usages - Using "dans" with streets and means of transportation (French Prepositions of Location)
entries.note: Added the bare named-street address after habiter and its transitive place-object alternative. Both habiter cette rue and habiter dans cette rue are accepted; general street-activity and regional-variation guidance remains intact.

references.purpose: The verb entry confirms both transitive place objects and prepositional location constructions; accept habiter cette rue as well as habiter dans cette rue.

entries.source_title: À + [heure] = At + [time] in French
entries.note: The distinction between telling the current time and locating an event with à is already explicit, including midi/minuit and contextual appointment items.

entries.source_title: Chez = at someone's place (French Prepositions)
entries.note: The existing person/profession/building contrast was good. Added chez nous versus à la maison and a physical-house viewpoint without declaring all possessive house phrases impossible.

entries.source_title: Compound nouns formed with prepositions à/de/en in French
entries.note: Added ingredient/flavour à and material de alongside en, qualifying a one-preposition-one-meaning shortcut while preserving the original purpose/contents contrast.

entries.source_title: Compound nouns formed with [noun] + à + [infinitive] in French
entries.note: Noun + à + infinitive already names function, keeps the infinitive unchanged and contrasts with an action's pour purpose; independent noun-group work makes the distinction usable.

entries.source_title: Telling time in French - general 12-hour clock rules
entries.note: Added explicit morning direct-minute readings beside conversational fractions. Do not import a categorical ban on quinze/trente/quarante-cinq below twelve; the existing hour agreement and moins patterns remain.

references.purpose: The full public time-writing guidance applies numerical hours and minutes throughout the day, including morning schedules; do not prohibit direct minute readings below twelve.

entries.source_title: Expressing numbers 70 to 999 in French
entries.note: The existing number-building method includes 71/81/91, cent/vingt agreement, feminine une and legitimate regional/hyphenation variants. Mapped production checks cover the actual spelling decisions.

entries.source_title: Expressing large numbers -thousands/millions/billions - in French
entries.note: Added quantity-noun millier(s) de versus invariable numerical mille, with the approximate ordinary-use perspective and direct noun linkage. Existing million/milliard and internal-number limits were retained.

entries.source_title: Writing decimal numbers in French
entries.note: Decimal notation and virgule reading were already worked through, but price reading lacked its own examples and assessment. Added spoken euro prices, value-preserving cents, currency agreement and a constrained written-price conversion.

entries.source_title: Telling time in French - 24-hour clock rules = AM vs PM
entries.note: Schedule and conversational readings were already separated. Added the boundary that direct minute counts also work in morning schedules, rather than treating the hour number alone as a grammatical prohibition.

references.purpose: The full public time-writing guidance applies numerical hours and minutes throughout the day, including morning schedules; do not prohibit direct minute readings below twelve.

entries.source_title: An vs année, matin vs matinée, jour vs journée, soir vs soirée to express a time unit or a duration in French
entries.note: The unit-versus-lived-period viewpoint already includes all four noun pairs, conventional greetings, age and the limit that numbers can accompany described années. No mechanical short/long word rule was needed.

entries.source_title: Ordinal numbers - 1st/2nd/10th/etc - in French
entries.note: Retained the already complete ordinal formation and acceptance of second/seconde when a series continues. The primary usage note confirms that the two-element distinction is optional, not a grading rule.

references.purpose: The primary usage note makes the two-element distinction optional; retain the published acceptance of second in a continuing series.

entries.source_title: Ordinal vs Cardinal numbers - Differences between French and English usages
entries.note: Added fraction tiers versus rank troisième and the first-ruler exception to cardinal name readings, with distinct contexts and independent production rather than an English ordinal calque.

entries.source_title: Expressing timeliness in French - late/early/on time - general
entries.note: Late/early/on-time expressions are already located against a schedule and contrasted with à temps and general tôt/tard; worked timing decisions and independent checks exceed a bare expression list.

entries.source_title: Expressing how you are with aller (Greetings in French)
entries.note: Added general well-being with aller versus a specific adjective state with être, including mieux and an answer that legitimately switches verbs after the greeting.

entries.source_title: Talking about the weather in French - il fait + [adjectif]
entries.note: Added pleasant-temperature bon versus pleasant-looking beau and the hot-object limit. Qualified the rejection of il fait soleil using the dictionary; our beginner models are not an exhaustive ban.

references.purpose: The dictionary records il fait (un beau) soleil, qualifying a blanket rejection of noun-based faire weather expressions.

entries.source_title: Talking about the weather in French - il y a + [nom]
entries.note: The noun-weather construction was already complete. Added le temps est venteux and retained established faire soleil, rather than importing claims that wind has no adjective or faire cannot occur with a noun.

references.purpose: The adjective entry and inflection table confirm that venteux exists for windy conditions; do not import a no-adjective-for-wind assertion.
The dictionary records il fait (un beau) soleil, qualifying a blanket rejection of noun-based faire weather expressions.

entries.source_title: Faire de/jouer à : talking about sports, hobbies and leisure activities in French
entries.note: Activity-dependent faire de/jouer à, contractions and legitimate overlap are already explicit and assessed. The ordinary-present teaching handles current versus habitual action without inventing a new tense for the activity noun.

entries.source_title: Jouer de = to play an instrument in French
entries.note: Instrument jouer de, all article shapes, game-versus-music contrast and common faire alternatives already have meaningful independent practice.

entries.source_title: Ça m'est égal = I don't mind/care (French Idiomatic Expressions)
entries.note: All six experiencer forms already retain singular est/égal, explain elision and distinguish no preference from dismissiveness. The actual public body revealed no missing core decision.

entries.source_title: Avoir besoin de = To need (French Expressions with avoir)
entries.note: Avoir besoin de already has a full model and contrasts mass, countable, identified and infinitive complements, with de/d' and contraction work.

entries.source_title: Avoir envie de = To feel like, want to (French Expressions with avoir)
entries.note: Added bodily-urge uses of envie so ordinary desire is not mistaken for a voluntary wish in every context; retained the existing noun/infinitive and article distinctions.

entries.source_title: Faire les courses vs Faire les magasins to talk about shopping (French Expressions with faire)
entries.note: Necessary shopping/errands versus browsing shops is already explained with the limit that visiting shops does not guarantee buying. Existing faire des courses nuance remains.

entries.source_title: Devoir vs Avoir besoin de to express "to need to" in French
entries.note: Added devoir + noun meaning owe, contrasted with needing a resource, plus bodily-urge evidence in the needs lesson. The prior obligation-versus-personal-need distinction was preserved.

entries.source_title: Expressing possession in French with "être à"
entries.note: Possession with être à and stressed owner pronouns already contrasts with noun-phrase ownership and keeps agreement with the possessed subject. Mapped production is sufficient.

entries.source_title: Être d'accord avec = to agree with (French Expressions with être)
entries.note: All être forms with invariant d'accord, avec + person/pronoun, topic sur and ordinary negation are already taught with independent responses.

entries.source_title: Avoir mal (à) = To be in pain, to hurt somewhere (French Expressions with avoir)
entries.note: Added common nausea interpretation of mal au cœur without a diagnostic claim, and the eye/eyes headword, elision and contraction contrast alongside existing body-part pain teaching.

entries.source_title: Describing senses with "sentir" - The different meanings of the verb "sentir" in French
entries.note: Added tasting-context sentir and a worked perceiver-versus-smell-source decision using the same construction; the existing reflexive self-state contrast remains available.

entries.source_title: Expressing ongoing actions in the present in French with "être en train de"
entries.note: The complete progressive expression already adds process emphasis rather than replacing every present, includes reflexives and distinguishes ongoing action from state, recent completion and future intention.

entries.source_title: Avoir peur de = To be afraid/scared of (French Expressions with avoir)
entries.note: Added feared-person stressed pronouns versus a subject-matched reflexive infinitive, with de/d' and original contexts. The existing noun-category contractions remain unchanged.

entries.source_title: Ça y est = That's it/It's done (French Idiomatic Expressions)
entries.note: The fixed expression already marks an expected point reached, including readiness and understanding rather than literal location, with context-sensitive independent responses.

entries.source_title: Ça ne fait rien = It doesn't matter (French Idiomatic Expressions)
entries.note: Minor-problem reassurance already contrasts with no preference, explains rien versus pas and recognises casual ne omission without imposing it in written tasks. Serious-concern limits are already explicit.
